name: The Palazzo Murena Cedar

location.address: Piazza dell'Universita 1 (cloister of Palazzo Murena, Rectorate of the University of Perugia)

verified_sources: data/registers/italy-masaf.json (sheet 12/G478/PG/10, girth 485cm, height 25m, Piazza Universita - Rettorato Centrale, Comune di Perugia municipal census of monumental trees, MASAF national register, CC BY 4.0)
access: Free, inside the cloister of Palazzo Murena, seat of the University of Perugia's Rectorate; the cloister is open to the public during normal building hours.
transport: Central Perugia, on Piazza dell'Universita just off Corso Vannucci; reachable on foot from Piazza IV Novembre in about 5 minutes, or via the Minimetro to Pincetto/Fontivegge then a short walk.
verify_notes: Carried over from an earlier verification pass (2026-08-08, parked when the course changed) and re-checked this pass, nothing new contradicts it. MASAF register: girth 485cm, height 25m. La Nazione (19 Sep 2021) independently measured the same cedar in Palazzo Murena's cloister at 5m trunk circumference, 30m tall, 35m crown diameter (slight measurement variance between sources, same tree, same site), estimated age 150-180 years, planted just after Italian Unification (1861) in the eclectic garden taste of the era. Survived a lightning strike, visible scars on trunk. Pruned and crown-consolidated by tree-climbing arborists (Associazione Alberi Maestri) in October 2010, after which trunk diameter grew 35cm. Health confirmed excellent by arborists in 2020. In 2020 trumpeter Paolo Fresu and accordionist Daniele di Bonaventura performed a concert titled 'Two for Tree' twelve metres up in its canopy, for environmental awareness. Strong anecdote to lead with: a 160-year-old cedar that hosted a jazz concert in its own crown.

https://guide.umbriaonline.com/news/cosa-vedere/piazza-italia.html (Piazza Italia, built after the demolition of the Rocca Paolina as a symbol of the post-Unification city, flowerbeds with 'remarkable century-old specimens of Atlas cedar and red fir')

verify_notes: Stands in the flowerbeds of Piazza Italia, one of Perugia's most prominent squares, built over the demolished 16th-century Rocca Paolina fortress as part of the post-Unification remaking of the city in the 1870s-80s. Tourism copy calls it a 'century-old specimen' without a precise year, alongside a red fir of similar age; girth 390cm, height 23m per the register. Strong witness angle: planted on ground where a hated papal fortress once stood, in the same decades the square itself was carved out of its ruins. Pairs naturally into a centro storico walk with pgi_001 (five minutes away) and the other cedars below.

name: The Holm Oaks of Giardini del Frontone

location.address: Giardini del Frontone, Borgo XX Giugno, Perugia

verified_sources: data/registers/italy-masaf.json (sheet 11/G478/PG/10, girth 350cm, height 15.5m; and sheet 10/G478/PG/10, girth 342cm, height 21.5m; both Giardini del Frontone, Perugia)

https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giardini_del_Frontone (public garden opposite the Abbey of San Pietro, laid out from 1707 for the Accademia degli Arcadi's summer gatherings, 18th-century avenues of monumental holm oaks, completed in the 1800s with pool, statues and plantings now centuries-old)

https://www.umbriacronaca.it/2025/05/14/perugia-20-giugno-1859-cosa-videro-i-secolari-lecci-del-frontone/ ('what did the secular holm oaks of the Frontone witness', 14 May 2025, ties the garden's veteran oaks to the 20 June 1859 sack of Perugia by papal troops)
transport: Borgo XX Giugno, about a 15 to 20 minute walk south of the centro storico, or a short bus ride.
verify_notes: Two of the garden's holm oaks are individually registered as monumental (350cm/15.5m and 342cm/21.5m, roughly 70m apart within the same gardens), folded into one entry since a visitor experiences the garden's oak avenues as a single destination rather than two separate stops. The gardens were laid out from 1707 for the Accademia degli Arcadi's literary summer gatherings, on ground used for military purposes from the 1400s and, before that, an Etruscan necropolis; crowned by the Arco del Frontone (1791). Strongest witness angle in this batch: a 2025 local history piece asks what these 'secolari lecci' saw on 20 June 1859, the day papal Swiss Guards and Antibes Legion troops sacked Perugia in the last major violence before Unification, a well-documented and significant event in the city's history. Confirmed alive and maintained (public gardens, actively described in current tourism and history copy). PIN: downgraded to approximate on merge; one point cannot mark two trees 70m apart, the same correction made to Amsterdam's Leidsebosje planes on 2026-08-08.
